resource: Retained explicit PostgreSQL SCRAM password/secret material
allocation_impact: Validate non-empty UTF-8 byte length from borrowed/already-bounded secret input before any retained String copy, formatting or SCRAM setup; checked aggregate arithmetic and same-root I reservation must succeed before allocation.
boundary_tests: 1024 UTF-8 bytes accepted when the secret is otherwise valid and all coupled retained-config checks pass
1025 UTF-8 bytes rejected as UNAVAILABLE before retained allocation or SCRAM work
Checked aggregate arithmetic overflow is rejected without logging secret bytes
notes: This is an Oteryn first-slice product ceiling, not a claim that PostgreSQL universally limits passwords to 1024 bytes. PostgreSQL 17 SCRAM supplies no smaller password-length contract; existing protected Oteryn password ingress uses a 1024-unit string ceiling, while this DB boundary deliberately uses the stricter allocation unit UTF-8 bytes.
